key_insight: A cell-centric, interpretable pathology framework (C3PRO) can match black-box multiple-instance learning models for PDAC diagnosis, survival, and resectability while exposing named histologic phenotypes.
clinical_relevance: This could help pathologists review model outputs with clearer visual and morphologic explanations, potentially improving trust and identifying novel prognostic tissue states.
method: Extracted embeddings from cell-centered tiles using a pathology foundation model.
Clustered embeddings into recurrent morphological phenotypes and built a spatial graph of phenotype motifs.
Benchmarked against multiple MIL models and had expert pathologists annotate representative phenotype mosaics.
evidence_signal: In a nested cross-validation cohort of 809 patients (825 biopsies), C3PRO achieved strong performance for diagnosis (AUC 0.958), survival (0.617), and resectability (0.696), comparable to top baselines.
watch_item: The phenotype vocabulary and prognostic signals need external validation and workflow testing before routine clinical use.
paper_title: An interpretable cell-centric representation of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma matches multiple-instance learning for clinical outcomes and leads to novel pathologist-driven histological biomarkers
